reviews.text: Feeling a tad peckish patiently awaiting the release of 'Slay the Spire 2'? If you enjoy deck builders and are a foodie, then this game offers a unique take on the dungeon crawling experience for a reasonable price. The monsters in these dungeons are hungry and as the princess of the castle, it is your job to whip them up tasty treats to save your kingdom. The British and Irish focused lore and meals added a really nice touch and some comical effect for me at least. Like mushy peas? Yall's CANNOT be for real rn...haha XD Honestly, this is a refreshing palate cleanser to the usual deck building models. Instead of doing damage to the monsters, you are trying to satisfy their hunger and figuring out their likes and dislikes, while also taking into consideration their cravings. You collect recipes and ingredients. Before venturing off you [i]cook[/i] up your deck before entering the dungeon, picking what dishes you want to bring along. Every dish has different flavour profiles and benefits. You can equip cookware offering different perks. Upon successfully satiating a monsters hunger, you collect loot varying from new recipes, gold and spices to amplify your dishes (wait, what… the British use spices?? >.> KIDDING LOL) Like other dungeon crawlers, you get to choose your pathway which triggers different events, so no run ever feels the same. This game is in EA but I haven't encountered any problems so far. It runs comfortably and flawlessly on the steam deck. I like how they have streamlined the buffs and ingredients, taking away a lot of cumbersome guesswork. When you collect ingredient rewards to restock your pantry, you get a choice of ingredients. Before you pick, it lets you know how many recipes in your deck currently use that ingredient. Similarly, as you apply buffs to the monsters by feeding them certain dishes, the "damage" on your cards is adjusted based on the existing buffs. Just nice QOL features and demonstrates attention to detail. My only complaint so far is that it seems a bit too easy. Some of the food buffs and the stacking of abilities seem overpowered. But the best part... is that you get a kitty companion. Food, cards and cats?? I am so there ^_^ Looking forward to seeing what this expands into, well done so far!! Update: if any features could be added, it would be nice if you could customize your character (and the cat too). In addition, I think that the likes and dislikes should be randomized every new run (or the monsters in the dungeons randomized) to keep the challenge aspect up. There is a certain level of predictibiity and it takes away from the fun. Once you discover the monsters likes and dislikes, it is easy to just construct specialized decks for that run because you know what monsters are in each dungeon.

[/quote] [b]Video Review TBD[/b] https://youtu.be/O77k5KLe9aA [h2]This Food Is ROTTAN![/h2] Full disclosure, I actually really like this game. This is a negative review mainly because Hungry Horrors becomes far too linear once you understand what you are walking into. Failure feels forced, not earned through player failure. Unless you already know which new creatures you are about to face and how they react to specific meals, they will walk all over you as it's all hard coded food interests. Your only real option is to slap Hard To Hate onto everything, which is not always possible, just to stop enemies from spitting out your food and deleting your run. In Hungry Horrors, you build a deck of meals and serve them to monsters before they decide to serve themselves with you. The problem is that progression is knowledge-gated. Even if you manage to build a strong deck, the game will eventually roadblock you until you brute-force information out of enemies. You are expected to throw food at monsters just to see whether they love, hate, or dislike it but you have 5-6-7 turns to do it and there are so many meals in the double digits. Once you learn that, future runs become manageable, but that discovery phase often comes at the cost of unavoidable failure. Outside of that issue, I genuinely enjoyed the game. It is comedic, occasionally challenging, and refreshingly simple. The core idea works, and when the systems line up, it is satisfying in a way that feels deliberate rather than overwhelming. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] Hungry Horrors is still in Early Access, which gives it room to grow, assuming that room is actually used. With better ways to communicate enemy preferences and less reliance on forced trial-and-error failure, this could turn into something special. If not, it risks becoming a game remembered more for its frustration than its charm. And if that happens, it might just earn itself a very strongly worded visit from Gordon Ramsay before it ever gets the chance to shine.

这款游戏在细节上很好，各种神话怪物有不同的背景故事 处决动画 食物喜好，被处决之后，回到城堡，猫猫还有对击杀你的怪物的评语。 但在玩法上就差很多了。 虽然是肉鸽卡牌 但卡组的构成里几乎没有流派差异，你要做的就是形成口味连招，然后祈祷对方不会特别讨厌这道菜。虽然单张卡有很多元素，但基本只要看口味和buff，而很多buff也只能做到锦上添花，没法作为核心，导致只能注重连招系统，让口味连贯，实际玩起来的决策部分很少，加上我不是英国和爱尔兰的民众，因此对菜本身看上去也没法共鸣【如果有什么麻辣烫-烤串-可乐的连招，看起来就不一样了】。 其次就是很多系统让人玩得不舒服，比如遗物系统，初始只能拿三个，多了的只能替换，而且扔掉旧的也没有收益；食谱要配合食材，有时候拿到了想试试看的食谱也会苦于没有食材不能做；功能型房间的类型太多了 宝藏 小角落 庇护所 任务 篝火 商店 ，初期经常不确定这些房间能干什么；房间和房间的怪物数值成长太快了，我第一次过了洞穴去森林，遇到的第一个木怪，走4步还和巨人的饱食度差不多，因此前期最好打几遍洞穴叠一下数值，但这又有前面的问题，游戏战斗的部分其实比较无趣，每把的差异化太小了，刷数值很无聊。 作为一个介绍英国神话怪物的游戏我觉得还可以，但作为构筑卡组的游戏我觉得不太合格，不过还是给个好评

英国真的有这么多菜嘛(￣▽￣)" 讲真，很难称呼这个游戏为卡牌游戏。卡牌(在这个游戏里是料理)的技能意义不大，口味(属性)才是王道。每张卡都有一个基本口味A，还有个出牌后生效的后续渴求口味B，只要卡组里味觉可以相互循环，不管是AB→BA→AB还是AB→BC→CA，那么卡牌本身的饥饿值(伤害)即可不断累加，每次成功接上味觉循环，那么之前循环的每张卡的伤害都可累加到这次出牌上，实现伤害的利滚利。唯一要注意的点就是怪物会有不喜欢和厌恶的料理(卡牌)，不喜欢会导致伤害累加里加进去一个0(其实还好)，厌恶则是会直接中断并清零伤害的累加，导致游戏崩盘被怪物斩杀。除此之外的所有系统（卡牌技能、肉鸽道具和天赋技能）都是服务于口味(属性)和饥饿(伤害)这两个数值 这就是这个游戏的全部玩法了，简单，轻松，配合自带吐槽的剧情和还算不错的画风和设定，可以一玩

深度很差，怪物机制差，但这是一个好的框架。 怪就这么几个动作，走路/攻击/增加大胃袋/犹豫，换皮然后加数值。 打牌这边菜品也没什么深度，口味连锁换地图就把菜从普通版换到稀有、史诗 遗物也就是厨具，限制格子玩起来不爽。 此游戏完全没有rogue的意思，更像是古老的RPG只是把回合制改成卡牌战斗了。 目前来说不推荐，只能说未来可期。喂食物给怪物这个点子可以给个好评，对比市面上大部分卡牌游戏好歹算是有点新意，但是这种作战方式并不新颖。。 加油
玩法简单易懂，拿料理喂怪物，说白了就是个DPS检测。不过比起游戏机制更有趣的是各种怪物的图鉴，传承出处等写的很详细，还有死亡动画也做了，不像现在大部分游戏都是黑屏以后回存档点。希望未来能打开创意工坊，让更多怪物，怪谈 传闻还有各国神话生物都往里面加

[h3](除了你)没有人会受伤的世界 [/h3] 做饭题材的卡牌构筑肉鸽游戏，与同类型的其他游戏相比，本作在设定上明显温柔不少，只要将怪物的肚子填饱即可过关和拿到奖励。 当然，要是在喂饱前被怪物打光了精力或是近身，作为主角还是会被以传统的方式干掉。 相比于其他卡牌构筑游戏里的攻击、防御、叠增益、上debuff、算伤害、过牌等一系列操作，饥饿怪物明显将战斗系统简化不少。 卡牌围绕甜、咸、酸、苦、鲜五个口味构筑，每道菜都有自己的口味和吃完后期待的口味，总体来说只要让手中牌能相互衔接上口味就可以。 不得不说当叠了四五条渴望链后的投喂还是挺爽的。 [h3]可惜不太肉鸽 [/h3] 即使有着新颖的设定和可爱的画风，本作的缺点也是显而易见的，太偏向于养成而非肉鸽。 可以说你很难做到像其他游戏一样天胡一把一路打通，一方面是基础菜系、道具甚至是血量都太过薄弱，需要依靠不断肝加成道具提升。 另一方面是游戏有一个增强代入感但惩罚极大的设定，一旦投喂了怪物不喜欢的食物，将会直接把先前的菜吐一大半并降低一大截饱腹度。 而怪物到底喜欢什么菜讨厌什么菜呢？只有通过一遍遍的试错后才能知道。 总的来说，EA阶段这个完成度还是蛮认可的，总体框架算有意思，期待后续优化和提升。 [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]
游戏其实还行，但每个场景就4种怪物，然后怪物饥饿值增长的有点过快了，第一个场景基础饥饿是50左右，到了第四个场景直接就1000+，叠渴望都叠不过来更别说初见还容易一发厌恶前面努力全白费

[H1]Feed the monsters or become the snack, simple rules[/H1] Clumsy Bear Studio really cooked with this one… alright, I’ll stop there. Jokes aside, I barely started playing yesterday and somehow ended up 9h30 later, having cleared the available content multiple times. For context, this is an early access review of version 0.1.6, played up to January 31st, 2025, and based on what’s currently in the game. Here’s the setup. You play a princess thrown into horror-filled worlds, and the way you survive encounters is by feeding the monsters until they’re full and no longer interested in your fleshy existence. Every creature pulls inspiration from British and Irish folklore, and the same goes for the meals you prepare. Each horror has its own food preferences, so you can’t just repeat the same recipe over and over. You build a starter deck, then adapt on the fly by chaining flavors and cravings. There are also seasonings, spices (yes, they’re different), ingredients, cookware, artifacts, and more. The result is a layered card-battler roguelike that’s easy to grasp and very satisfying to master. So far, 5 out of the planned 8 realms are available, with 3 still missing along with the big final boss. Even at this stage, there’s a lot to do. The pixel art is adorable, the princess’ idle animations are genuinely funny, and every death has its own little animation. There’s a bestiary that tracks monster preferences, and once you learn them, they show up directly on the cards, which is extremely helpful. Progress carries over between runs through gold, ingredients, potions, quest items, and knowledge, so replaying realms actually makes you stronger. You can revisit any completed realm as much as you want in the same run, speed things up with 2X movement and combat, play with mouse or keyboard, and quit runs safely thanks to regular saving. Recipes unlock steadily, with new ingredients added each time you clear a realm for the first time, and achievements are simple, progression-based, and limited to the current content. Completionists should just keep in mind that more achievements will likely appear as updates roll out if the devs keep the sam eachievement pattern. I also really like the overall ambiance and the main antagonist’s attitude, which adds a nice layer of personality to the whole thing. That said, some rough edges show up once you’re deep into it. To progress smoothly, you’re strongly encouraged to replay previously cleared realms multiple times to farm resources, especially since encountering new enemies and their preferences is pure luck. At first it’s fun, but after two or three realms, it starts to feel repetitive. Epic cookware and potions drop very rarely, and once your deck is already functional, the loop turns into farming for the sake of farming. It gets old fast. Either making new monster encounters easier to avoid farming, increasing enemy variety, or limiting how many times a realm can be replayed per run could help keep things fresher (I think that 4-5 times a realm per run is a nice sweet spot. Enough to gather ressources, but not too many repetitions either). There are also some bugs. Meal upgrades don’t always show properly at the seasoning station, which leads to confusion and loss of time. Boss intro animations can’t be skipped and become repetitive if you play in loops. Taking screenshots with Steam Layout is awkward because key presses advance dialogue too quickly, especially frustrating if you try to catch end-of-run stats. On top of that, there are a few minor issues like brief mouse control hiccups that clearly need polish, nothing major, but noticeable. Even with those flaws, this is a very solid indie roguelike for fans of supernatural lore, clever systems, and funny characters. The princess can get a bit annoying, sure, but that’s forgiven the moment you realize you can pet the cat (almost) endlessly. I’m genuinely curious to see how this grows over time and can’t wait to dive back in when new realms drop. 最刺激的莫过于 做菜好几轮 还差一个回合就赢了 结果怪物全吐了…… 肉鸽+料理的组合真的很好玩 整体框架非常好 感觉未来可期 所以给个推荐 希望多打磨打磨系统

说实话，玩到这游戏的时候，我还真被它的设定惊艳了，不同于市面上大多肉鸽牌组游戏要么打怪升级、要么闯关解谜的套路，这游戏扮演公主，靠做传统料理，去喂饱怪物。你的攻击的方式不是战斗，就是把这些怪物喂到满意、自行消失，既能保命，还能顺着剧情继续往前走，这种设定真的太新鲜了。 核心玩法，坦白说，它本质上还是一款肉鸽以及牌组构建的游戏，整体大框架和同类型游戏差不太多，比如随机生成的关卡、局内收集资源等等。但创意够特别，玩起来完全不觉得枯燥，整体体验下来很舒服。 最让我觉得有意思的，是它的牌组和其他牌组游戏靠打怪抽卡、攒卡牌不一样，这款是靠战斗收集食材，再用食材去烹饪已有的食谱，做出的食物才是你的卡牌。 所有卡牌都围绕着六种口味转：酸、甜等，还有一个比较特别的无味。怪物吃了某一种口味的食物后，会对另一种口味产生兴趣。只要你能一直喂怪物当下喜欢的口味，连锁效果就不会断，每喂一次，前面所有的连锁效果都会一起触发，有时候运气好，一套连锁就能直接喂饱一只怪物。怪物对不同口味也有偏好。 还有一个很特别的点，游戏里的怪物没有血量条！取而代之的是饥饿值和行走步数。我们的目标就是用食物把它们的饥饿值喂满，只要喂饱了就算通关了。 总的来说，最亮眼的就是它新颖的题材和设定，如果你本身就喜欢肉鸽游戏，或者对牌组构建类感兴趣，又想找一款不那么同质化、有新鲜感的游戏，这款真的可以入手试试，不会让你失望的。 [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]

This game is quite fun and also very unique. But there is one thing that made me very sad: that old man was killed by the witch while protecting me. I would give a good review and even invite my friends to play this game if you could let the old man come back to life in the end. That old man taught me what sacrifice and protection mean, and that even the weakest person can protect others. I want to say thank you to him. If the old man ends up dying in the end, I will cry while changing my positive review to a negative one, because he was like my late grandfather.

[h1]First impressions[/h1] Something unique, but has low amount of content, for about 4-6 hours. What is there actually quite polished and playable - you cook to find monster's loves and likes while trying to avoid dislike and hates. Potions allows you to change many things and manipulate difficulty, so eventually you will win no matter what. Do not expect level of Slay The Spire 2 early access variety, this is very small game. [h1]Gameplay[/h1] Changing deck is difficult, you can add cards, but they mostlikely won't synergize with current deck, so you end up with a lot of cards and no clue how to turn them into something good. Sure there is ability to delete cards, but that will not help at all, cus you need working build at all times and can't just 'delete legs or hands from human to switch for a horn and tail'. Later as you accumulate potions and special ingredients it is possible to greatly change dish, like making them ignore monster preference or multiplying whole dish chain by %, which kind-a breaks game. There is not much content and variety, similar items popping up early-game over and over, also they do not scale into higher areas. This is understandable for early access, but compared to other EA games like Against The Storm had, this one feels more like demo. Progression system between runs fully changes balance, you have to grind it to get forward. Like, it does make difference between starting with basic 10 HP or 25+, considering some monster hit for 9+. Or getting 40 gold per kill instead of zero. Many monsters and dishes have no passives, making it really boring, and good half of passives only viable pre world 5 (like +5 hunger to monster per turn against 3000 life sponge). There is also bad spice scaling system which requires starting from world 1 to gather spices and boost dmg of dishes. But each spice only boost by +1 and only specific dish ingredient, so again, it is hard to make a smart build unless you 'cheat' with universal chain flourish dishes. [h1]Final thoughts[/h1] I do like uniqueness of this game, story, humor, visuals, gameplay... But balance and little amount of content are concerning, it will take a lot of effort to turn it into something acceptable by nowdays standarts. Devs going to finish EA in about 1 year, so lets see how they add content and scale everything as time goes on. Majority have 6-10 hours of playtime and never returned to game after writing positive review, so bear in mind.

People often describe the most menacing beasts as having insatiable hungers, be that for violence or evil. In Hungry Horrors, the monsters are very satiable, and you’ll only succeed by feeding them.
Charming, vibrant cooking adventure with rich folklore and fun co-op for all ages, though predictable foes and linear late-game play cap replay value.
Gather ingredients, make dishes and feed all the strange creatures in a deck-builder that manages to set itself apart from the others in Hungry Horrors.
